scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario did the right thing by making a Facebook post about their best friend without telling him. Let me break this down step by step. First, the friend went on a three-month trip to India to volunteer, building a water pipeline and teaching kids about hygiene. That's a pretty significant and positive thing he did. He paid for the trip himself, which cost over $3000, so it's a big deal financially too. The friend is described as shy and quiet, so it makes sense that he wouldn't share this information with many people on his own. The person in question, who is 22F, decided to make a Facebook post about her friend's trip because she thought he needed recognition. She did this while he was away, about a week before he came back. Since he was in India without internet, he didn't see the post until he started traveling home. When he got back, she went to the airport to welcome him, along with his parents. He seemed annoyed but didn't say much, and when she tried to hang out, he declined, saying he wanted to rest. Later, he texted her to express his anger about the post, saying he didn't want attention and that the trip was more for self-improvement than volunteering. He felt the post was unnecessary and that she shouldn't have done it without asking, especially since he wouldn't see it for a week. So, the question is: Was she AITA (Ask If Trolling Allowed) for making that post? I think the key points here are about consent, privacy, and the friend's intentions. She made the post without asking him, assuming he wouldn't tell people himself because he's shy. But he clearly didn't want the attention and felt that the post misrepresented his reasons for going. She thought it was a nice thing to do, but he felt it was intrusive and unnecessary. I can see both sides. On one hand, she wanted to recognize his good work and share it with others who might not know. On the other hand, he didn't want that attention and felt that his reasons were more personal, not meant for public recognition. She knew he was shy, so she might have thought he wouldn't do it himself, but she didn't ask him if he was okay with it. Another point is that she posted while he was away, knowing he couldn't respond or see it immediately. That might have added to his frustration because he couldn't address it in real-time. He had to deal with the aftermath when he got back, which could have made him feel ambushed. So, considering all this, I think she overstepped by posting without his consent. Even though her intentions were good, respecting his privacy and his wishes is more important. He made it clear he didn't want the attention, so she should have respected that.
